material_systems.name: PVA Drywall Primer
material_systems.description: Polyvinyl acetate (PVA) primer for bare drywall walls. Economical, fast-drying, excellent sealing of porous drywall surfaces. Standard choice for new construction.

products.notes: PVA-based primers seal porous drywall and provide good holdout for topcoats. Zero stain blocking — sealer only (RC-002). Low VOC, water cleanup.

material_systems.name: Acrylic Latex Primer
material_systems.description: Premium acrylic latex primer for new drywall walls. Superior adhesion, better hide, excellent topcoat holdout. Recommended for QT4 work.

products.notes: Acrylic latex provides better adhesion and build than PVA, and better topcoat compatibility. Zero stain blocking — sealer only (RC-002).

material_systems.name: High-Build Drywall Primer
material_systems.description: High-build primer for Level 5 finish or when maximum wall surface uniformity is required. Fills minor imperfections.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec 500 Interior High Build Primer
products.notes: High-build formula fills minor imperfections and provides uniform porosity across joints and field. May require light sand before topcoat.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Bare drywall wall, proper application thickness, standard porosity
Level 3 has more exposed paper, higher absorption, lower coverage
Texture increases surface area, reduces coverage 15-25%
High-build applied at greater thickness, lower coverage by design

consumables.name: 18-inch roller 3/8" to 1/2" nap

consumables.notes: 18-inch roller typical for spray+backroll production. 3/8" to 1/2" nap for smooth drywall. 9-inch acceptable when obstacles prevent 18-inch.

consumables.notes: 1/2" nap for orange peel and knockdown textures. Do NOT use 3/4" nap for knockdown — 3/4" is only for stomp/popcorn or porous masonry.

consumables.specification: 9-inch standard roller cover, 3/8 to 1/2 inch nap range, synthetic blend
consumables.notes: 3/8" to 1/2" nap for smooth drywall walls. Replace per product change or after ~5000 SF.

consumables.name: 9-inch roller 1/2" nap (textured)
consumables.specification: 9-inch standard roller cover, 1/2 inch nap, synthetic blend
consumables.notes: 1/2" nap for textured wall surfaces (orange peel, knockdown). Do NOT use 3/4" nap for knockdown.

consumables.name: Rosin paper
consumables.notes: Full floor coverage for hard floors during wall spray. Taped seams required. Not needed on subfloor (RC-003).

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting 1.5 mil
consumables.specification: 1.5 mil plastic sheeting for floor protection
consumables.notes: Full floor coverage for carpet during wall spray. Taped edges required.

consumables.name: Masking tape 1.5-inch
consumables.notes: For taping floor protection seams and fixture covers. 180 LF (60 yards) per roll. NOT used for ceiling masking — we do not mask drywall ceilings.

consumables.name: Outlet/switch covers
consumables.specification: Plastic fixture covers or masking film squares
consumables.notes: Covers for electrical outlets and switches during spray. Estimate ~6 per room average.

consumable_notes.ceiling_masking: We do NOT mask drywall ceilings when spraying walls. We either cut in at the ceiling line (roll method) or spray directly into the wall-to-ceiling corner (spray+backroll when ceiling is primed). Only millwork ceilings would require masking.
consumable_notes.roller_nap_warning: Do NOT use 3/4" nap for orange peel or knockdown textures. 1/2" nap is correct. 3/4" nap is only for stomp/popcorn texture or very porous masonry (concrete block, CMU).
consumable_notes.roller_size_flexibility: 18-inch roller is typical for spray+backroll but 9-inch is acceptable when obstacles prevent 18-inch use (closets, tight spaces, around fixtures).
